### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), /meta/flow/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/data-service.mdx`  _(via /api/protocol.zod (route, a path literal on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), getMetaItemCached (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), /api/protocol.zod (route, a path literal on a changed line))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface), ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), /meta/flow/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via IAutomationService (symbol, a top-level interface), registerFlow (symbol, a method of class AutomationEngine), /meta/flow/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `34b0e4901de4bec3e596fd7e69a63ae5c626da6c` — the merge of head `93a72727a561114fadc0693c491962d04431f4fc` into base `18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 34b0e4901de4bec3e596fd7e69a63ae5c626da6c && git checkout 34b0e4901de4bec3e596fd7e69a63ae5c626da6c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 93a72727a561114fadc0693c491962d04431f4fc && git checkout -B drift-repro 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 && git merge --no-ff 93a72727a561114fadc0693c491962d04431f4fc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b84fe5552ad42271d6ff4e12dcb9f1425abb208`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23316 (body; triage `6152874675`, claim `6153420029`, amendment `6157354342`, seat 2's pointer `6157680240`, the dev report `6158808801`, the seat ACCEPT `6158838703`, the last as a claim under test, not evidence); PR #23358 (body, the one bot comment, 22-file list, net diff against `main`); the check-runs on the head; `origin/main` at `707b3cd91e4cf33c3d0d46b012852e25beb1360c` (merge base `6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8`); #23317's branch head `ac768f1d54f1225d9cb6e64b581ca0fe8312774d`; objectui on disk at `7578323`, read only. Every tree read was by sha (`git show SHA:PATH`, `git grep … SHA`). Nothing was built, run or checked out.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The ruling, the premise, the ban — held.**
- *Envelope sibling of `lock`, never inside `item`.* `getMetaItem`'s final envelope spreads `registration` beside `lock` / `editable` / `version` (`protocol.ts` about `:11153`); the REST cached branch spreads it into the `{ type, name }` envelope, and `translateMetaEnvelope` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:3062`) spreads the envelope and puts the document under `item`, so it cannot land inside the body. Pinned on the item read (`read.item` has no `registration`), the cached read and the list.
- *The closed set is total and real.* `FlowRegistrationSchema` is a `discriminatedUnion('state')` of exactly `registered`, `refused` (with `reason` REQUIRED, `{ message, code? }`) and `unregistered`; a fourth state and a reason-less `refused` are pinned refused. `AutomationEngine.getFlowRegistration` is total over its own state: `flows.has(name)` → `registered`, `flowRefusals.has(name)` → `refused`, else `unregistered`. So `unregistered` is a real engine answer — the complement, not a made-up third state — and `reason` is the thrown error's own `message` (and its string `code` only when set), copied verbatim; the integration pin asserts byte equality with what `registerFlow` throws for the same body.
- *Absence documented as "never `registered`".* Both schema members' docblocks and `.describe` strings, `flows.mdx` and the changeset say so. Absence is produced where ruled: no automation service or none declaring the member (`resolveFlowRegistrationReader` returns `undefined`), every non-flow type (`canonicalMetaType(type) !== 'flow'`; REST additionally guards `metaType === 'flow'`), a draft read (both the `readState === 'draft'` return and the `previewDrafts` draft-hit return precede the final envelope; the list skips `_draft: true`), and the execution face (`audience !== 'served'`). Each is pinned on the protocol double.
- *The seam is existing, with the named precedent.* `this.getServicesRegistry?.().get('automation')` is the constructor-supplied accessor (`protocol.ts:6644`), read lazily per call exactly as `resolveFlowCanonicalizer` (`:6537`) reads `canonicalizeStoredFlow`. `packages/metadata-protocol/package.json` on the head declares no `service-automation` dependency, and `git grep service-automation` over `packages/metadata-protocol/src` (tests excluded) hits only three comments. The member lives on the existing `IAutomationService` contract, optional, beside `canonicalizeStoredFlow` and `getFlowRuntimeStates`; the engine registers itself under `automation` (`plugin.ts:975`).
- *The bans hold.* The diff touches no write path in `protocol.ts` (reads only), no `status` enum, no stored row; `engine.ts` / `plugin.ts` add in-memory records only. The warn line `[Automation] cold-boot flow bind: failed to register flow` and the #21848 `withdrawFlow` call are context lines, byte-unchanged; the warn's level stays `warn`.

**(b) Recording correctness — correct, with one dormant path noted in ③.**
- Three recording sites, the three the dev names: the `kernel:ready` bind (`plugin.ts:2611`, AFTER the #21848 withdrawal, so the record outlives the withdrawal's own `flowRefusals.delete`), the `metadata:reloaded` re-sync (`:2527`) and the mutation sync (`:2751`). The boot pull in `start()` (`:1384`) catches, warns and records nothing — the startup-registry rule honoured; `check:startup-registry-verdict` runs on CI in `Lint · docs & code guards` (`lint.yml:3049`), green on the head.
- *Held and refused at once: impossible.* `recordFlowRefusal` returns early while `flows.has(name)`; `registerFlow` deletes the record immediately after `flows.set` (`engine.ts:4520`); `withdrawFlow` deletes it (`:4651`), and `unregisterFlow` delegates to `withdrawFlow`. The bind's order (withdraw, then record) is the right one.
- *A stale `refused` surviving a successful registration:* no reachable path. The only other `flows.set` site is `rollbackFlow` (`engine.ts:5779`), which does not clear the record — but it requires `flowVersionHistory` for the name, which `withdrawFlow` deletes and which `registerFlow` pushes only after every validation has passed, so a name the engine refused and holds nothing under has no history and `rollbackFlow` throws before `flows.set`. Dormant, not reachable; flagged in ③ for the next `flows.set` site.
- *The out-of-scope note (a refused re-save of a held flow):* pre-existing. The keep ("the engine keeps the registration it had") is #21725's behaviour on `main`; this PR adds no keep and serves `registered`, which is literally what the schema defines (a registration under the name). It can mislead a reader into assuming the served body is the registered one. Proportion: the save door's `runtime-authoring-gate` mirrors the engine's checks branch for branch, so reaching that state needs drift between the two, and the dev measured no door that accepts such a body; #23317 narrows the drift further by making registration's checks the one list the stored pass previews. Not this PR's defect and not blocking; a docblock precision for the seat, in ③.

**(c) The cached REST branch (the amendment) — verdict live, never stored, never in the ETag; A as shipped.**
- `getMetaItemCached` performs the delegate `getMetaItem` on EVERY call (it is a validator wrapper, no store) and takes `registration` from that result; the hash is over `JSON.stringify(item)` plus the locale only, so the verdict is in no validator. The `If-None-Match` arm is gated `&& registration === undefined`, so a judged read is never answered `notModified`; the return adds `registration` only when defined. Pinned: same ETag with and without an engine; judged read not 304, unjudged control still 304.
- At REST, for a `flow` the mask posture is `OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_NOT_APPLICABLE` (`kind: 'passthrough'`, no `runtime`), `intakeFolds` and `audienceFolds` are false, so `If-None-Match` is handed to the protocol (which ignores it for a judged flow) and REST's own folded-ETag 304 comparison does not run. `cachedRegistration` is spread into both `res.json` exits of the branch (the undetermined-posture exit and the normal one); the 304 exit cannot be reached with a verdict present. Nothing is stored anywhere. No stale verdict can be served.
- Unjudged flows and every other type: `registration` is `undefined` at the protocol (non-flow types never resolve a reader) and `cachedRegistration` is `{}` at REST, so their 304 behaviour and their cached envelope are byte-identical; pinned at REST (`page/home`).
- `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` is now `MetadataCacheResponseSchema.extend({ registration: optional })`: additive, optional, every existing key and default untouched; the generated reference shows the one added property. Correct.

**(d) The list — as ruled.** `getMetaItems` returns `{ type, items, …registrations }` with BARE items (`flowRegistrationsOf` reads the names of `governed` and mutates nothing); one entry per listed item whose `name` is a string and which is not `_draft: true`; served audience only. `createMetaListAnswer` is the one chain both transports call (`rest-server.ts:6106`, `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:587`), and every step rewraps through `withItems`, which spreads the raw envelope — sibling keys survive on both. The per-caller list gate judges `app` / `dashboard` / `view` / `object` / `book` / `doc` and returns every other type as given, so `flow` lists are unaffected. The list route reads `getMetaItems` directly (no cached list branch), so the default door serves `registrations`.

**(e) Pins — the real composition, with controls; ablations directionally consistent, one count not.** `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts` boots `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` (its metadata protocol on `driver-sql` / better-sqlite3 `:memory:`) + `AutomationServicePlugin`, lands two `sys_metadata` rows and the node executor from a later plugin's `start()` (after the boot pull), so the `kernel:ready` bind is the judge; it pins the item read, the cached read, the list, a registered control, and a corrected save clearing the refusal. The REST pin asserts the cached branch (`getMetaItemCached` called, `getMetaItem` not) with registered and other-type controls; the protocol double pins no-service, no-member, `view`, draft, execution-face and 304 controls. Ablation 2 (REST spread removed: 2 red / 1 green over a 3-case file) matches the tree. Ablation 1 (bind recording removed: "2 failed / 2 passed") does NOT match the 5-case file on the head, where three cases read the refusal (item, cached, list) — see ③.

**(f) Semver and docs — true and minimal.** See ②. `flows.mdx` ("Discovery & Registration") states the three states, the ending of `refused`, absence, the live-read / never-304 behaviour and the per-process scope, each true of the code. `variant-docs.json` binds `state:refused|registered|unregistered` to `flows.mdx` in the existing key convention; the alias pins move 776 to 778 with both prose counts updated; the generated references (134 to 136 protocol schemas, 1524 to 1526 total, 434 to 436 API) and the strictness count (438 to 442: the refusal object plus three union arms) are consistent with the four new `z.object` sites. Nothing beyond what the gates owe.

**(g) Overlap with #23317 (`ac768f1d5`) — textual adjacency, no semantic collision.** #23317 edits `engine.ts` (`registerFlow`'s four validate calls become a `registrationChecks` loop that throws `new Error(refusal.message)`; `canonicalizeStoredFlow` splits into `canonicalizeFlow` plus a lazy `todos` getter) and `automation-service.ts` (the `canonicalizeStoredFlow` docblock only, lines 802 to 825). It touches no `plugin.ts`, `protocol.ts` or `protocol.zod.ts`. #23316's hooks sit at `registerFlow`'s success tail (`flows.set` then `flowRefusals.delete`), in `withdrawFlow`, and in two new members — none moved by #23317. Because #23317 keeps `registerFlow` throwing the same message (its changeset says so; the checks threw plain `Error`s before and `new Error(message)` after, neither with a `code`), the verbatim `reason` this PR records is unchanged whichever lands second. Seat 2 already renamed its refusal types apart from `FlowRegistration` (`377dc370b`). Whichever lands second re-runs the automation suite, as `6157680240` records.

**(h) CI on the head, read once at `2026-10-14T01:47:02Z`.** 44 check runs: 33 success, 8 skipped (the opt-in and path-filtered gates: `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood matrix shards, `Temporal Conformance`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, and the duplicate `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` entries), none failed, and three **in progress at read**: `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)` — the only non-green checks. `Test Core (2/6)`, `(5/6)` and `(6/6)` are green; so are `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, every `Lint ·` lane, `Type Check · source gates`, `· consumer gates`, `· workspace`, `· debt ledger` and the `TypeScript Type Check` aggregator, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the claim guards. The gates the dev left NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is an unconditional step of `Build Core` (`ci.yml:2643`, no `if:`), which ran and is green — measured by CI; `check:type-check-debt` is the re-measure step of `Type Check · debt ledger` (`lint.yml:6152`, `continue-on-error` behind a `Lane verdict` step that keeps a red gate red), which ran and is green — measured by CI. `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` is in `packages/spec/vitest.repo-tests.json` (the 59-file `repo` project), which `Test Core` runs whole through `turbo run test test:repo`; whether it ran in full is decided by the shard that carries `@objectstack/spec`, and three shards were still in progress at read, so it is **not yet confirmed by CI at this read**. This verdict is conditioned on those three shards landing green; a red one re-opens it.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23316-refused-flow-registration-verdict.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/rest` — all `minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Correct: the repo is in changesets pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`: `mode: pre`, tag `next`; all four at `18.0.0-next.0`), AGENTS.md rules `yes` takes at least `minor`, and each package publishes something new — spec: four exports and three optional response fields plus an optional contract member; metadata-protocol and rest: a served field; service-automation: two public engine members. No arm narrows, nothing is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. Every sentence of the changeset is true of the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Ablation 1's count predates the cached-read pin.** The report's "2 failed / 2 passed" fits a four-case file; the head's integration file has five cases, three of which read the refusal. The direction (recording removed turns the item read and the list red) is proven and the cached read is covered by ablation 2 and by its own assertion against the real producer, so the evidence stands — but the count is not the head's. A re-run at the head would read 3 red / 2 green.
2. **A refused flow's record outlives its row.** The bind deletes a refused name from `syncedFlowNames`, so when that row is later deleted the mutation sync's delete arm `continue`s before `withdrawFlow`, and `flowRefusals` keeps the entry. No reader sees it (the item read 404s, the list keys only listed items) and re-creating the name clears or re-records it, so it is a bounded leak of one string per deleted refused flow. Noted, not blocking.
3. **`rollbackFlow` is a `flows.set` site that does not clear `flowRefusals`.** Unreachable for a refused name today (no version history survives a withdrawal or a refusal), so no defect; the next `flows.set` site must clear the record or route through `registerFlow`.
4. **`registered` names a registration, not the served body (the dev's out-of-scope finding, read as pre-existing).** On a refused re-save of a held flow the engine keeps the older body and the read serves the newer one beside `registered`. Pre-existing keep; the `registered` arm's docblock could say "a registration under the name, not necessarily this body". Seat's call; no door measured to accept such a body.
5. **Declared deviations, all inside the claim's lines:** the contract member (one of the premise's seam forms), `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` + `getMetaItemCached` (the amendment's "same seam"), `variant-docs.json` and the alias pins (gate-owed), recording widened to the reload and mutation syncs (same files, the boot pull deliberately excluded), and option A for 304s (the seat answered A in `6158838703`; the amendment's "never part of the ETag" is kept literally). No stored-row stamp, no new status value, no field inside `item`.
6. **objectui follow-up (H5), confirmed read-only at `7578323`:** `flow-problems.ts:375` `deriveFlowRunStatus` falls back to the stored `status` with no runtime reading, so a refused `active` flow renders `enabled`; `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:6412` feeds the `_status` row (`null` for a refused flow, read as `unpublished`). No console surface reads `registration`. The seat files it, per the claim.
7. **The cached branch's missing protection envelope** (`lock`, `version`, `editable`, …) is pre-existing and declared open in `GetMetaItemResponseSchema`'s docblock; not this card's, per the amendment.
8. **The per-caller list gate and `registrations`:** `withItems` keeps the map while the gate prunes items, which is moot today (`flow` is ungated) but a future flow list gate must prune `registrations` to the served items.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `93a72727a561114fadc0693c491962d04431f4fc`
Local-runs: none

Delta review over the prior at-tier record `6159075428` (PASS on `2b84fe5552ad42271d6ff4e12dcb9f1425abb208`, read in full; its judgments (a)–(h) and flags 1–8 stand and are not re-rendered). Scope: only what changed between `2b84fe555` and `93a72727a` beyond `main`'s own content, and whether the PR's behaviour is byte-unchanged. Inputs read: PR #23358 (body, both comments, the 22-file net diff against `main`); card #23316's six comments (nothing posted after the seat ACCEPT `6158838703`); the check-runs on the head, read once at `2026-10-14T02:53:54Z`; read-only git by 40-hex sha — the prior base `6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8`, `main` at `18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` (the merge's second parent; `git merge-base` of head and main), the merge commit `ba00d5942475c6eb4d0adebf7cb29b69cbd4fef6`, #23348 at `707b3cd91e4cf33c3d0d46b012852e25beb1360c`. Nothing built, run, re-run or checked out.

### ① Derived judgments

**Shape of the delta.** `93a72727a` = `ba00d5942` (a true merge: parents `2b84fe555` and `18cd410dc`, both verified as ancestors) + one regen commit whose whole diff is `content/docs/references/index.mdx` (5 insertions, 4 deletions). `main` landed ten PRs in `6d96721fa..18cd410dc` (#23303, #23313, #23349, #23326, #23346, #23257, #23353, #23348, #23345, #23283); #23317 is not among them. The PR still touches no governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green).

**(1) Behaviour unchanged — held, byte-exact.** The `+`/`-` lines of `git diff 6d96721fa 2b84fe555` and of `git diff 18cd410dc 93a72727a`, per file with hunk headers and context stripped, are identical for 20 of the 22 files: `protocol.ts` (81 lines), `rest-server.ts` (17), `engine.ts` (59), `plugin.ts` (17), `protocol.zod.ts` (111), `automation-service.ts` (26), the changeset (15), `flows.mdx` (18), `protocol.flow-by-name-shipped-name.test.ts` (159), `meta-flow-cached-registration.test.ts` (121), `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts` (196), `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts` (53), `variant-docs.json` (8), `references/api/protocol.mdx` (125), the strictness ledger `api.md` (2), and the five `packages/spec/*/api.json` projections (4 / 5 / 4 / 4 / 2). The only two files whose lines differ are the hand-kept alias pin file (16 lines before, 17 after — judged in (2)) and the generated `index.mdx` (10 and 10, different numbers — judged in (3)). No difference to name on any non-generated, non-registration file. No conflict marker in any of the 22 files on the head. `main`'s own `protocol.ts` change (#23345) survives: the head-versus-main diff of that file is exactly the PR's 81 lines.
